units.title: Result<T>
units.description: Domain methods return Result / Result<T> instead of throwing for expected failures.

units.title: Outbox
units.description: Integration events are stored with the data, in the same transaction, and delivered by a background processor with retries.

units.title: Inbox
units.description: Each integration event handler runs once per message, even when the message is delivered again.

units.title: Request validation
units.description: FluentValidation validators check the shape of requests before the handler runs; the domain stays the authority.

units.title: Repository / unit of work
units.description: Handlers use a repository per entity and IUnitOfWork, defined in Core, instead of AppDbContext.

units.title: CQRS
units.description: Endpoints send commands and queries to handlers in the slice; queries read without tracking.

handlers.title: Own handlers
handlers.description: A small dispatcher in the solution, no package.

mediator.title: Mediator
mediator.description: The source-generated Mediator package (MIT), with the same interfaces.

units.title: Idempotency keys
units.description: A retry with the same Idempotency-Key header gets the stored response instead of running the action again.

units.title: SQL Server
units.description: SQL Server, in a container from the AppHost or an existing server.

units.title: PostgreSQL
units.description: PostgreSQL, in a container from the AppHost or an existing server, with snake_case names.

units.title: Redis
units.description: Redis behind IDistributedCache and HybridCache, shared by every instance; in a container from the AppHost.

license.notice: Redis 7.4 and later are source-available (RSALv2 / SSPLv1), and Redis 8 adds AGPLv3. The container is fine for development; check the terms before production, or use Valkey (see docs/caching.md).

units.title: FusionCache
units.description: FusionCache (MIT) runs HybridCache: fail-safe, timeouts, and with Redis a backplane that keeps every instance up to date.

units.title: RabbitMQ
units.description: Integration events go through RabbitMQ: sent after the commit (or by the outbox), retried, then dead-lettered; in a container from the AppHost.

units.title: Azure Service Bus
units.description: Integration events go through an Azure Service Bus topic: sent after the commit (or by the outbox), retried, then dead-lettered; the emulator runs locally from the AppHost.

license.notice: Azure Service Bus is a paid Azure service. The local emulator (AppHost and tests) runs under Microsoft's emulator license terms, accepted for you by the AppHost and the tests; it is for development only.

units.title: Keycloak
units.description: Every endpoint requires a login: the API validates Keycloak's tokens, with realm roles as role claims; the AppHost runs Keycloak with a ready realm and test users.

units.title: Microsoft Entra ID
units.description: Every endpoint requires a login: the API validates Entra ID tokens for your app registration, with app roles as role claims; the AppHost asks for the tenant and client IDs.

license.notice: Microsoft Entra ID is an Azure service: you need a tenant and an app registration (the free tier is enough for development). The tests don't call Entra; they sign their own tokens.

units.title: ASP.NET Core Identity
units.description: Every endpoint requires a login: the API stores its own users (register, login and account endpoints under /account) and issues bearer tokens; roles as role claims, an admin role seeded.

units.title: SignalR
units.description: Push messages to connected clients (a user, a group, everyone) through one hub; messages for changes wait for the commit and are dropped if the save fails.

units.title: Soft delete
units.description: Deleting an entity sets DeletedAt instead of removing the row; deleted rows are hidden from every query, and the API answers as after a real delete.
units.addNote: existing entities aren't converted: add ISoftDeletable and a DeletedAt property to the ones that need it, then create the migration (see docs/soft-delete.md).
